text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis continues his visit to Britain.
- The cabinet accepted and sent to parliament the draft of a new customs law, elaborated in line with EU principles.
- The cabinet accepted and sent to parliament a bill which envisages giving free port status to Ventspils.

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele announced in Copenhagen that the Baltic states have no other alternative to guarantee their security but to join NATO. His counterparts from Denmark and Iceland announced their support to Latvia's attempts to join the alliance.

- The board of nationalist party Fatherland & Freedom announced that renouncing the peace treaty which Latvia concluded with Soviet Russia in 1920 means legalising the Soviet annexation of Latvia in 1940 and its consequences.

- A spokesman for Russian President Boris Yeltsin said in an interview to the Russian-language Latvian newspaper SM that Russia admits introducing economic sanctions against former Soviet republics, including Latvia, to secure the rights of the Russian-speaking population in these countries.
- The deputy head of NATO forces in Europe, General Jammerson, is visiting Latvia. He said the alliance would help the Baltics approach its standards.
- Police found a secret drug manufacturer in one of Riga's new districts. They confiscated 65 kg of poppy seeds and eight litres of extraction fluid used to produce drugs.

- On December 12, shareholders of Unibanka, Latvia's largest bank, will discuss a possible merger with Latvia's sixth largest bank, Zemes Banka. The merger is supported by the Latvian government and the EBRD, which is a shareholder in both banks.

- A group of weapon repair specialists from the Latvian state-owned company Arsenals have designed a new assault rifle which, they believe, is good enough to be exported abroad for use by special units such as Marines.
